senses.title: Remove a false belief

senses.why: A rainbow sheen fading off a soap bubble.

intro.en: Disillusion is dis- plus illusion; illusion comes from Latin illusio, a mocking or deceptive appearance, from illudere, to play with, from in- plus ludere, to play.
intro.cn: disillusion 由 dis-（去掉）加 illusion（幻觉）构成；illusion 来自拉丁语 illusio「嘲弄、假象」，来自 illudere「戏弄」，由 in- 加 ludere「玩」组成。

items.en: Latin ludere means to play.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为玩。

items.en: Illudere meant to play with or mock.
items.cn: illudere 意为戏弄、嘲弄。

items.en: Illusio meant a mocking or a deceptive appearance.
items.cn: illusio 意为嘲弄或骗人的外观。

items.en: Illusion entered English for a false appearance.
items.cn: illusion 进入英语，表示虚假的外观。

items.en: Dis- gave disillusion, to take the illusion away.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disillusion，意为把幻觉拿走。

items.en: The verb became common in writing about lost ideals.
items.cn: 这个动词在关于理想破灭的论述中变得常见。

note.en: Disillusion is illusion with the false appearance removed; its neighbours share the play root or mean correcting belief.
note.cn: disillusion 是把假象拿掉的 illusion；它的邻居要么同「玩」词根，要么指纠正信念。

senses.example: The plastic does not disintegrate in seawater.

senses.whyCN: 一个被标记的原子在探测屏上不断抛出碎块。

intro.en: Disintegrate is dis- plus integrate; integrate comes from Latin integrare, to make whole, from integer, untouched and so whole, from in- plus tangere, to touch.
intro.cn: disintegrate 由 dis-（分开）加 integrate（整合）构成；integrate 来自拉丁语 integrare「使完整」，来自 integer「未被触碰的、完整的」，由 in- 加 tangere「触碰」组成。

items.en: Latin tangere means to touch.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tangere 意为触碰。

items.en: Integer meant untouched, hence whole.
items.cn: integer 意为未被触碰的，因此是完整的。

items.en: Integrare meant to make whole again.
items.cn: integrare 意为使重新完整。

items.en: Integrate entered English for making into a whole.
items.cn: integrate 进入英语，表示合成整体。

items.en: Dis- gave disintegrate, to break the whole apart.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disintegrate，意为把整体拆散。

items.en: The word gained a use in radioactive decay.
items.cn: 这个词获得了放射性衰变方面的用法。

note.en: Disintegrate is integrate reversed; its neighbours share the whole root or mean falling apart.
note.cn: disintegrate 是 integrate 的反向；它的邻居要么同「完整」词根，要么指散开。

definition_zh: n. 分离；分裂；（逻辑）析取；不一致

intro.en: Disjunction is dis- plus junction; junction comes from Latin junctio, a joining, from jungere, to join or yoke, the root behind join, joint and conjunction.
intro.cn: disjunction 由 dis-（分开）加 junction（连接处）构成；junction 来自拉丁语 junctio「接合」，来自 jungere「连接、套轭」，也是 join、joint 与 conjunction 的词根。

items.en: Latin jungere means to join or yoke.
items.cn: 拉丁语 jungere 意为连接、套上轭。

items.en: Junctio meant a joining or a joint.
items.cn: junctio 意为连接或接合处。

items.en: Old French jonction carried the sense of a joining.
items.cn: 古法语 jonction 带有连接的意思。

items.en: Junction entered English for a place where things meet.
items.cn: junction 进入英语，表示事物相接之处。

items.en: Dis- gave disjunction, a state of being unjoined.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disjunction，指未连接的状态。

items.en: The logical sense of or became standard in the subject.
items.cn: 表示「或」的逻辑义成为该学科的标准用法。

note.en: Disjunction is junction opened; its neighbours share the join root or name things coming apart.
note.cn: disjunction 是被打开的 junction；它的邻居要么同「连接」词根，要么指事物分开。

intro.en: Dislocation is dis- plus location plus -ion; location comes from Latin locatio, a placing, from locare, to place, from locus, a place, the root behind local and locate.
intro.cn: dislocation 由 dis-（离开）加 location（位置）加 -ion 构成；location 来自拉丁语 locatio「安置」，来自 locare「放置」，词根 locus「地方」，也是 local 与 locate 的来源。

items.en: Latin locus means a place.
items.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为地方。

items.en: Locare meant to place or set.
items.cn: locare 意为放置、安置。

items.en: Locatio meant a placing or a lease.
items.cn: locatio 意为放置或租约。

items.en: Location entered English for a place or position.
items.cn: location 进入英语，表示地点或位置。

items.en: Dis- gave dislocate, to put out of place.
items.cn: dis- 造出 dislocate，意为使离开原位。

items.en: Dislocation became the standard term for a joint injury.
items.cn: dislocation 成为关节损伤的标准用语。

note.en: Dislocation is location moved away; its neighbours share the place root or name things shifted out of order.
note.cn: dislocation 是离开原位的 location；它的邻居要么同「地方」词根，要么指事物被挪出秩序。

intro.en: Dismay comes from Old French desmaier, from dis- plus esmaier, to frighten, which goes back to a Germanic root magan, to be able, so it once meant to deprive of power.
intro.cn: dismay 来自古法语 desmaier，由 dis- 加 esmaier「使惊恐」组成，上溯日耳曼语词根 magan「能够」，所以本义是「把力量与勇气拿掉」。

items.en: A Germanic root magan means to be able.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 magan 意为能够。

items.en: Exmagare meant to deprive of power.
items.cn: exmagare 意为剥夺力量。

items.en: Esmaier meant to frighten or discourage.
items.cn: esmaier 意为使惊恐、使气馁。

items.en: Desmaier added dis- for a stronger shock.
items.cn: desmaier 加上 dis-，表示更强的惊愕。

items.en: Dismay entered English for loss of courage.
items.cn: dismay 进入英语，表示失去勇气。

items.en: The noun sense of shock and sadness follows.
items.cn: 表示震惊与难过的名词义随后出现。

note.en: Dismay is power taken away; its neighbours share the able root or name sudden loss of heart.
note.cn: dismay 是被拿走的力量；它的邻居要么同「能够」词根，要么指突然失去心气。

intro.en: Dismiss comes from Latin dimittere, to send away, made of dis-, apart, and mittere, to send.
intro.cn: dismiss 来自拉丁语 dimittere（遣散），由 dis-（分开）与 mittere（送）构成。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go.
items.cn: mittere 指送出或放开。

items.en: Dimittere meant to send people away in different directions.
items.cn: dimittere 指把人往各处遣散。

items.en: Desmettre meant to put away or release.
items.cn: 古法语 desmettre 指放走、解除。

items.en: English dismiss meant to send away a crowd.
items.cn: 英语 dismiss 指遣散一群人。

items.en: The sense of removing from a post became common.
items.cn: 免职这一义在十九世纪通行。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dismiss stem, and the meaning group names other ways of pushing someone out.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dismiss 词干，近义组列出别的把人推开的方式。

sensesIntro.cn: 被打发走：盒子里的工牌、桌边的提案与合上案卷旁的法槌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a notice on a desk with a badge put into a box while a gavel comes down beside a closed file
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一张通知书、工牌被收进盒子，同时法槌在合上的案卷旁落下

branches.en: A worker sent out with a badge in a box.
branches.cn: 工牌收进盒子被送走的工人。

branches.en: A plan pushed to the edge of the table.
branches.cn: 被推到桌边的方案。

branches.en: A case closed by a falling gavel.
branches.cn: 被落下的法槌结束的案件。

branches.en: Both send something away from attention.

branches.en: Both end without a full hearing.
branches.cn: 两者都不经完整审理就结束。

intro.en: Dismissal is dismiss plus -al; the send root also builds mission, transmit, emit and remit.
intro.cn: dismissal 由 dismiss 加 -al 构成；送这个词根也造出 mission、transmit、emit 与 remit。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere means to send, dimittere to send away and missio a sending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere 意为送，dimittere 意为送走，missio 意为派遣。

definition_zh: v. 不服从；违抗；违反（命令、规则）
definition_en: to refuse to do what a person, rule or command tells you to do
core_image: 红灯亮着，一辆车却径直开过去；教官喊停，队列里一个人继续往前走
scene: 他违抗了直接命令。He disobeyed a direct order.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：命令明确，他却偏偏不照做。

senses.title: Refuse a command
senses.definition: to refuse to do what a person in authority tells you
senses.definitionCN: （动词）拒绝照掌权者的话去做
senses.example: He disobeyed a direct order.
senses.exampleCN: 他违抗了直接命令。
senses.why: A soldier walking on while the officer calls halt.
senses.whyCN: 教官喊停，队列里一个人继续往前走。

senses.title: Break a rule
senses.definition: to act against a rule or law
senses.definitionCN: （动词）做出违背规则或法律的行为
senses.example: Drivers who disobey the sign are fined.
senses.exampleCN: 违反这个标志的司机会被罚款。
senses.why: A car going straight through a red light.
senses.whyCN: 一辆车径直闯红灯。

senses.title: Ignore guidance
senses.definition: to fail to follow advice or instructions given for your good
senses.definitionCN: （动词）不遵从为你好而给出的建议或指示
senses.example: She disobeyed the doctor and kept working.
senses.exampleCN: 她不听医生的话，继续工作。
senses.why: A prescription left unopened beside a laptop.
senses.whyCN: 一张没拆的处方放在笔记本电脑旁。

intro.en: Disobey is dis- plus obey; obey comes from Old French obeir, from Latin oboedire, to listen to, from ob- plus audire, to hear, the root behind audio and audience.
intro.cn: disobey 由 dis-（否定）加 obey（服从）构成；obey 来自古法语 obeir，上溯拉丁语 oboedire「听从」，由 ob- 加 audire「听」组成，也是 audio 与 audience 的词根。

items.en: Latin audire means to hear.
items.cn: 拉丁语 audire 意为听。

items.en: Oboedire meant to listen to, hence obey.
items.cn: oboedire 意为听从，因此是服从。

items.en: Old French obeir carried the sense of obeying.
items.cn: 古法语 obeir 带有服从的意思。

items.en: Obey entered English for doing as told.
items.cn: obey 进入英语，表示照吩咐去做。

items.en: Dis- gave disobey, to refuse to obey.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disobey，意为拒绝服从。

items.en: The word covers orders, rules and advice.
items.cn: 这个词涵盖命令、规则与建议。

note.en: Disobey is obey with the hearing refused; its neighbours share the hear root or mean open resistance.
note.cn: disobey 是拒绝去听的 obey；它的邻居要么同「听」词根，要么指公开抗拒。

entries.definition: to do what a person or rule tells you

entries.definition: the act of refusing to obey
refusing to do as told
to openly resist or refuse to obey
to break a rule, law or agreement
to openly show contempt for a rule

definition_zh: 混乱；失调
definition_en: a state in which things are not in order, or an illness of body or mind
core_image: 一屋子椅子全翻了，没有一把在原位
scene: 椅子全被推翻，桌上的纸页散了一地。The room was left in complete disorder.
sceneCN: 这里 disorder 指「混乱」（第 1 个义项：没有秩序的状态）；句意是房间被弄得一片混乱。

senses.title: A lack of order
senses.definition: a state in which things are not arranged or controlled
senses.definitionCN: 事物没有排列好或失去控制的状态
senses.example: The room was in complete disorder.
senses.exampleCN: 房间一片混乱。
senses.why: Chairs on their backs draw a map of a hurried exit.
senses.whyCN: 翻倒的椅子，画出一张匆忙离开的地图。

senses.title: An illness of body or mind
senses.definition: an illness that affects the normal working of the body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 影响身体或精神正常运作的病症
senses.example: He was treated for a sleep disorder.
senses.exampleCN: 他因睡眠失调接受治疗。
senses.why: A system out of order inside a body is still called disorder.
senses.whyCN: 身体里失去秩序的系统，也叫失调。

intro.en: Disorder is dis- plus order, from Old French desordre and Latin ordo, a row or arrangement.
intro.cn: disorder 是 dis- 加 order；order 经古法语 desordre 上溯拉丁语 ordo（行列、排列）。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, a rank or an arrangement.
items.cn: ordo 指行列、等级或排列。

items.en: Dis- before a noun marked the loss of that arrangement.
items.cn: 名词前的 dis- 标出这种排列的失去。

items.en: Desordre meant confusion and lack of order.
items.cn: 古法语 desordre 指杂乱与失序。

items.en: English used it for a broken arrangement of things.
items.cn: 英语用来指事物排列被打乱。

items.en: Medicine gave it the sense of a body system out of step.
items.cn: 医学又给了它身体系统失调这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on order, and the meaning group names other states of confusion.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 order 构成，近义组列出别的混乱状态。

entries.definition: an arrangement or a command
not working in a normal way
noisy and hard to control
a state of complete confusion
a state where nothing is clear
a problem of the body or mind

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a chair on its back and end with a body out of rhythm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一把翻倒的椅子开始，落到一具失去节奏的身体。

normal.en: Dis- plus order: order is gone.
normal.cn: dis 加 order，秩序没了。

normal.en: One fallen chair is an accident; ten are a disorder.
normal.cn: 一把椅子倒下是意外，十把倒下就是混乱。

normal.en: A desk in disorder hides the one paper you need.
normal.cn: 乱桌上总藏着你要的那一张纸。

normal.en: A sleep disorder is a clock inside the body gone wrong.
normal.cn: 睡眠失调，是身体里的钟走错了。

normal.en: Disorder in a street is a matter for the police.
normal.cn: 街上的秩序混乱，要交给警察。

abstract.en: Picture ten chairs lying on their sides.
abstract.cn: 想象十把椅子侧倒在地上。

abstract.en: Picture papers spread from desk to door.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页从桌边铺到门口。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with hands moving at odd speeds.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的指针快慢失常。

examples.en: The room was left in complete disorder.
examples.cn: 房间被弄得一片混乱。

examples.en: He is being treated for a sleep disorder.
examples.cn: 他正在接受睡眠失调的治疗。

examples.en: The storm threw the whole schedule into disorder.
examples.cn: 暴风雨把整个日程打乱了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disorder 记成「没有次序」：dis 是否定，order 是秩序；东西不在次序里就是混乱，身体里的次序乱了就是失调。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加名词 order 构成；order 来自拉丁语 ordo（行列、排列），经古法语 ordre 进入英语。本义是排列被打乱，后来医学又用它指身体或精神系统失去正常节律。

sensesIntro.en: From a room out of order to a body out of step with itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个失序的房间，到一具与自身节奏错开的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chairs on their backs and papers across the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：椅子翻倒，纸页铺满地面。

branches.en: The first sense is the room that has lost its plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是失去布局的房间。

branches.en: The second sense is the body that has lost its rhythm.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是失去节律的身体。

branches.en: Both senses describe a system without its usual order.
branches.cn: 两个义项都形容失去平常秩序的系统。

branches.en: Both can be caused by one sudden event.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能由一件突发的事引起。

branches.en: Only the second sense is treated by a doctor.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项由医生处理。

intro.en: Disorder stands opposite order, inside the Latin ordo family of rows and ranks.
intro.cn: disorder 与 order 相对，属于拉丁语 ordo（行列与等级）一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo, a row or arrangement, gives order; the prefix dis- removes the arrangement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ordo（行列、排列）给出 order，前缀 dis- 把排列拿走。

items.example: A disorderly crowd filled the square.
items.exampleCN: 一群喧闹失控的人挤满广场。

items.example: The disorderliness of the desk was famous.
items.exampleCN: 那张桌子的凌乱很出名。

items.example: An ordered row of jars stood on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 架子上排着一列整齐的罐子。

items.example: She reordered the shelves by height.
items.exampleCN: 她按高度重新排了架子。

items.example: The queue moved in an orderly way.

definition_zh: v. 使失去方向感；使迷惑；使迷失
definition_en: to make someone lose their sense of direction or feel confused
core_image: 一个人站在没有路标的岔路口，手里的地图被转了个方向；走廊尽头的门牌全被换过
scene: 大雾让徒步者失去了方向感。The fog disoriented the hikers.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：大雾让徒步者分不清东西南北。

pos.zh: 使失去方向感；使迷惑；使迷失

senses.title: Lose physical direction
senses.definition: to make someone unable to tell which way they are facing or going
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让某人分不清自己朝哪个方向、往哪里走
senses.example: The fog disoriented the hikers.
senses.exampleCN: 大雾让徒步者失去了方向感。
senses.why: A hiker at a fork with no signpost and a turned map.
senses.whyCN: 一个徒步者站在没有路标的岔路口，地图被转了方向。

senses.title: Confuse the mind
senses.definition: to make someone unable to think clearly about a situation
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让某人无法清楚地理解处境
senses.example: The sudden change disoriented the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 突如其来的变化让全队摸不着头脑。
senses.why: A corridor whose door plates have all been swapped.
senses.whyCN: 一条门牌全被换过的走廊。

senses.title: Lose bearings in time
senses.definition: to make someone lose their sense of time or place after a shock
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让人在冲击之后失去对时间或地点的感觉
senses.example: Waking in the dark disoriented him for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 在黑暗中醒来让他一时分不清身在何处。
senses.why: A bedside clock read upside down in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗中倒着看的床头钟。

intro.en: Disorient is dis- plus orient; orient comes from Latin oriens, the rising sun and so the east, from oriri, to rise, the root behind origin and original.
intro.cn: disorient 由 dis-（去掉）加 orient（确定方位）构成；orient 来自拉丁语 oriens「升起的太阳、东方」，来自 oriri「升起」，也是 origin 与 original 的词根。

items.en: Latin oriri means to rise.
items.cn: 拉丁语 oriri 意为升起。

items.en: Oriens meant the rising sun, hence the east.
items.cn: oriens 意为升起的太阳，因此指东方。

items.en: Old French orient carried the sense of the east.
items.cn: 古法语 orient 带有东方的意思。

items.en: Orient entered English for facing east or finding bearings.
items.cn: orient 进入英语，表示朝东或确定方位。

items.en: Dis- gave disorient, to take the bearings away.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disorient，意为把方位感拿走。

items.en: The sense widened to mental confusion.
items.cn: 词义扩大到心智上的迷惑。

note.en: Disorient is orient with the bearings removed; its neighbours share the rise root or mean leaving someone puzzled.
note.cn: disorient 是把方位感拿掉的 orient；它的邻居要么同「升起」词根，要么指让人困惑。

dict_mnemonic.text: disorient ＝ dis-（去掉）＋ orient（确定方位，拉丁语 oriens「升起的太阳、东方」，来自 oriri「升起」，与 origin、original 同根）＝把参照的太阳拿掉，「使失去方向感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hiker at a fork with no signpost holding a map turned the wrong way while door plates are swapped down a corridor

branches.en: Hikers in fog with no sun to follow.

branches.en: A team facing swapped door plates.

branches.en: A clock read upside down in the dark.

branches.en: Both leave the mind without a fixed point.

intro.en: Disorient is dis- plus orient; the rise root also builds origin, original and orientation.

latinIntro.en: Latin oriri means to rise, oriens the east and fundere to pour.

intro.en: Disorientate is disorient plus the verb suffix -ate, a longer British form; the base goes back to Latin oriens, the rising sun, from oriri, to rise.

items.en: Dis- gave disorient, to take the bearings away.

items.en: British usage added -ate to give disorientate.

items.en: Both forms are accepted, with disorient commoner in American English.

definition_zh: 散布；扩散；分散；传播
definition_en: the act or process of spreading things out over a wider area, or the state of being scattered in different directions
core_image: 蒲公英种子被风一吹，从一处散向整片河谷
scene: 秋天，蒲公英的种子被一阵风带离母株，散落到河谷各处。 In autumn, dandelion seeds are carried away from the parent plant by a gust of wind and undergo wide dispersal across the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 dispersal 是「散布、扩散」（第 2 个义项：生物繁殖体的传播）；句意：秋天，蒲公英种子被一阵风吹离母株，散布到河谷各处。

pos.zh: 散布；扩散；分散（多作不可数；指一次具体扩散过程时可数）

derivatives.zh: 可分散的；可溶解分散的

senses.title: Scatter outward from one point
senses.definition: the process by which things that were gathered in one place move apart and cover a wider area
senses.definitionCN: 原本聚在一处的东西分开移动、覆盖更大范围的过程
senses.example: The dispersal of the swarm began when the queen left the hive.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂群随着蜂王离巢而开始散开。
senses.why: Latin dispergere joins dis- 'apart' to spargere 'to strew, scatter'. The prefix does the work of separation, so the noun names the outward breaking-up of a group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dispergere 把 dis-「分开」与 spargere「撒、铺散」结合；前缀本身承担“分离”的动作，因此这个名词指群体向外散开的过程。

senses.title: Biological seed or spore spread
senses.definition: the movement of seeds, spores, or larvae away from the parent organism to new places
senses.definitionCN: 种子、孢子或幼体离开亲本、到达新地点的过程
senses.example: Wind dispersal lets maple seeds colonize clearings far from the parent tree.
senses.exampleCN: 风力传播让枫树种子在远离母树的空地上定殖。
senses.why: Once spargere is applied to living propagules, the 'strewing' becomes sowing: the plant scatters its seeds exactly as a hand scatters grain, and the distance travelled is what the term measures.
senses.whyCN: 当 spargere 用于活体繁殖体时，“撒开”就变成了“播种”：植物像手撒谷粒一样把种子撒出去，而这个词度量的正是种子移动的距离。

senses.title: Population dispersal: individuals leave a group
senses.titleCN: 种群扩散：个体迁出群体
senses.definition: the movement of individuals away from a crowded or natal population into new areas
senses.definitionCN: 个体离开拥挤的或出生的种群、进入新区域的移动
senses.example: Dispersal reduces competition because young animals leave the densest ranges.
senses.exampleCN: 扩散能减轻竞争，因为幼兽会离开最密集的活动范围。
senses.why: The same outward scatter is read as a demographic event: what moves is not grain but individual animals, and the result is a new distribution of the species.
senses.whyCN: 同一种向外散开被读作种群事件：移动的不是谷粒而是动物个体，结果是该物种形成新的分布。

senses.title: Physical or chemical dispersion
senses.titleCN: 物理化学意义上的分散
senses.definition: the spreading of particles, molecules, or droplets through a medium so that they are no longer clumped
senses.definitionCN: 颗粒、分子或液滴在介质中铺开而不再聚集
senses.example: Ulasonic stirring produces a fine dispersal of clay particles in water.
senses.exampleCN: 超声搅拌使黏土颗粒在水中形成细微分散。
senses.why: In the laboratory the Latin image becomes literal: spargere describes particles strewn through a liquid, and the noun names the resulting non-clumped state.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，这个拉丁意象变成字面意义：spargere 描述颗粒被撒进液体，名词则指由此得到的非聚集状态。

senses.title: Dispersal of a crowd or gathering
senses.definition: the breaking up of an assembled crowd, often because it is told or forced to leave
senses.definitionCN: 聚集人群的解散，常因被要求或被强制离开
senses.example: The dispersal of the crowd took less than ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的散开不到十分钟就完成了。
senses.why: A crowd is a gathering held in one place; dis- pulls it apart in all directions, so the nominal form describes the moment the assembly stops being an assembly.
senses.whyCN: 人群是聚集在一处的集合；dis- 把它向四面八方拉开，因此名词形式描述集会不再成为集会的那个时刻。

senses.title: Spread of information or ideas
senses.definition: the spreading of knowledge, news, or beliefs to many people or places
senses.definitionCN: 知识、消息或观念传播到许多人或许多地方
senses.example: Printing enabled the rapid dispersal of scientific ideas across Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术使科学观念在欧洲迅速传播。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from physical scattering to information: ideas leave one mind and are strewn among many, and the word keeps the same outward direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻从物理撒散延伸到信息：观念离开一个头脑、撒布到许多人之间，词义保持同样的向外方向。

senses.title: Decentralization of power or resources
senses.definition: the distribution of authority, money, or functions away from a single center
senses.definitionCN: 权力、资金或职能从单一中心向外分配
senses.example: The dispersal of authority to regional offices weakened the capital's control.
senses.exampleCN: 把权力下放到地区办事处削弱了首都的控制。
senses.why: Here what was held at one center is scattered to several points. The Latin separation is political rather than physical, but the shape of the movement is identical.
senses.whyCN: 这里原本集中在一处的东西被散到若干点。拉丁语中的“分离”是政治性的而非物理性的，但移动的形状完全相同。

senses.title: Forced scattering: police dispersal
senses.definition: the clearing of a crowd or gathering by authorities, sometimes with force
senses.definitionCN: 当局对人群或集会的清场，有时使用武力
senses.example: The police ordered the dispersal of the illegal demonstration.
senses.exampleCN: 警方下令驱散这次非法示威。
senses.why: When an authority does the scattering, the neutral 'spreading out' acquires a coercive edge; dis- is imposed on the crowd from outside rather than happening by itself.
senses.whyCN: 当驱散由当局执行时，中性的“散开”带上了强制色彩；dis- 是从外部强加于人群，而不是人群自行散开。

intro.en: Dispersal is a nineteenth-century noun built on the older verb disperse, which came through French from Latin dispergere. The date is approximate; the underlying PIE root is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: dispersal 是 19 世纪在较早的动词 disperse 基础上构成的名词；disperse 经由法语来自拉丁语 dispergere。年代为大致估计，最底层原始印欧词根属于重构。

items.en: The noun dispersal is recorded from the 1820s in the sense 'act of dispersing', formed by adding the native suffix -al to the verb disperse.
items.cn: 名词 dispersal 于 19 世纪 20 年代被记录，义为“分散的行为”，由动词 disperse 加本族后缀 -al 构成。

items.en: The verb goes back to Latin dispersus, past participle of dispergere 'to scatter, disperse'.
items.cn: 该动词可追溯到拉丁语 dispersus，即 dispergere「撒开、分散」的过去分词。

items.en: dispergere = dis- 'apart, in different directions' + spargere 'to strew, sprinkle, scatter'. The same spargere gives sparse, intersperse and aspersion.
items.cn: dispergere = dis-「分开、向不同方向」+ spargere「撒、洒、散布」。同一个 spargere 还产生 sparse、intersperse、aspersion。

items.en: Spargere is traced to a reconstructed root *sper- 'to strew', also seen in Greek speirein 'to sow' and sperma 'seed'. The reconstruction is conventional rather than directly attested, so the deepest layer is source uncertain.
items.cn: spargere 被追溯到重构词根 *sper-「撒播」，同样见于希腊语 speirein「播种」与 sperma「种子」。这一重构是通行做法而非直接证据，故最深层来源不确定。

items.en: Old French disperser and its participle gave English the verb in the 14th century; English later coined the noun rather than borrowing a Latin noun.
items.cn: 古法语 disperser 及其分词在 14 世纪把该动词带入英语；英语后来是自己造出名词，而不是借入拉丁名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps two nouns: dispersal for the process, especially in biology and planning, and dispersion for physical scattering such as light dispersion.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两个名词：dispersal 指过程，尤其在生物学与规划领域；dispersion 指物理上的分散，如光的色散。

entries.definition: the physical scattering of light or particles; also a statistical spread. It is the Latin-derived sibling of dispersal.
entries.definitionCN: 光或粒子的物理分散；也指统计离差。它是 dispersal 的拉丁式同源名词。

entries.definition: the act of getting rid of something, from dispose (dis- + ponere 'to place'). It has nothing to do with scattering.
entries.definitionCN: 处理、处置的行为，来自 dispose（dis- + ponere「放置」）。与“撒散”无关。

entries.definition: thinly spread; not dense. It descends from Latin sparsus, the participle of the same spargere.
entries.definitionCN: 稀疏的；不密集的。它来自拉丁语 sparsus，即同一个 spargere 的分词。

entries.definition: a substance that keeps particles apart in a liquid; a product noun from disperse.
entries.definitionCN: 使颗粒在液体中保持分离的物质；由 disperse 构成的产品名词。

entries.definition: the action of throwing things in many directions. It is plainer and more physical than dispersal.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西向多方向抛散的动作。比 dispersal 更朴素、更偏物理。

entries.definition: the slow spreading of particles, heat, or ideas through a medium. It stresses gradual mixing rather than an initial scatter.
entries.definitionCN: 粒子、热量或观念在介质中的缓慢铺开。强调逐渐混合，而非最初的散开。

entries.definition: the act of extending over a wider area. It is the neutral everyday word that dispersal formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展到更广区域的行为。是 dispersal 所正式化的日常中性词。

entries.definition: the way things are placed or shared across an area or group. It names the result, while dispersal names the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 事物在某区域或群体中的放置或分配方式。它指结果，dispersal 指移动过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases, and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- means apart and spargere means to strew: dispersal is literally 'strewing apart'.
normal.cn: dis- 表示“分开”，spargere 表示“撒”：dispersal 字面就是“撒开”。

normal.en: Seed dispersal is the standard term in ecology for how plants move their seeds away from the parent.
normal.cn: seed dispersal 是生态学中表示植物把种子送离母株的标准术语。

normal.en: Dispersion is the physics cousin: light dispersion through a prism spreads colours apart.
normal.cn: dispersion 是物理学中的同源词：棱镜中的光色散把颜色分开。

normal.en: Sparse and intersperse share the same spargere root: sparse is 'scattered thin', intersperse is 'scatter between'.
normal.cn: sparse 与 intersperse 共享同一个 spargere 词根：sparse 是“撒得稀”，intersperse 是“撒在中间”。

normal.en: Police dispersal is the coercive branch: the crowd is scattered by order, not by wind.
normal.cn: police dispersal 是强制分支：人群是被命令驱散的，不是被风吹散的。

abstract.en: Picture one handful of grain released above a field: the hand opens, the grains separate in the air, and the pattern widens as they fall. That widening is dispersal.
abstract.cn: 想象一把谷粒在高处松开：手张开，谷粒在空中分离，落下时分布越来越宽。这个“变宽”就是 dispersal。

abstract.en: The same shape applies to seeds, animals, particles, ideas, and authority: something once held at one point is released to many points.
abstract.cn: 同一形状适用于种子、动物、颗粒、观念与权力：曾经集中在一点的东西被释放到许多点。

abstract.en: Dispersal is the movement, distribution is the final map; keeping the two apart prevents circular definitions.
abstract.cn: dispersal 是移动过程，distribution 是最终地图；把两者分开可以避免循环定义。

examples.en: The study tracked seed dispersal by attaching radio tags to wind-borne fruits.
examples.cn: 这项研究通过给风力传播的果实装上无线电标签来追踪种子扩散。

examples.en: Habitat loss blocks dispersal and leaves populations isolated in small patches.
examples.cn: 栖息地丧失阻断扩散，使种群被隔离在小块斑块中。

examples.en: The dispersal of the protest began only after the mayor's announcement.
examples.cn: 示威的驱散是在市长宣布之后才开始的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地斯破手”——地上一撒，破开的手一扬，种子向四方散开 → dispersal 分散、传播

root: 拉丁语 dispergere「向不同方向撒开」，由 dis-（分开）+ spargere（撒、散布）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of dispersal, all one gesture: what was gathered at a point is released and widens outward, whether it is seeds, animals, particles, a crowd, news, or authority.
sensesIntro.cn: dispersal 的八个义项都源于同一个动作：原本集中在一点的东西被释放并向四周变宽——无论那是种子、动物、颗粒、人群、消息还是权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opens above a field and the grains separate as they fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在田野上方张开，谷粒落下时彼此分开。

branches.en: SIMPLE SCATTER: objects or a crowd break apart in all directions.
branches.cn: 简单散开：物体或人群向四面八方分开。

branches.en: LIFE: seeds and animals leave the parent or natal group and reach new habitat.
branches.cn: 生命：种子和动物离开亲本或出生群，抵达新栖息地。

branches.en: MATTER: particles are strewn through a medium and stop clumping.
branches.cn: 物质：颗粒被撒入介质，不再聚集。

branches.en: ABSTRACT FLOW: ideas and authority move from one center to many points.
branches.cn: 抽象流动：观念与权力从单一中心流向多个点。

branches.en: FORCE: an authority imposes the scatter on a crowd from outside.
branches.cn: 强制：当局从外部把“散开”强加于人群。

intro.en: Dispersal is the verb disperse plus the noun suffix -al. Inside the verb, dis- is the only living prefix; spargere is a Latin verb stem, not a productive English element.
intro.cn: dispersal 是动词 disperse 加名词后缀 -al。动词内部只有 dis- 是仍可分析的活前缀；spargere 是拉丁动词词干，不是能产的英语成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin spargere 'to scatter' supplies sparse, aspersion and intersperse beside the dispergere family; the modern Greek seed words sperm and spermat- descend from a related but separate speirein.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spargere「撒」除了 dispergere 一族，还提供 sparse、aspersion、intersperse；现代希腊语系的 sperm、spermat- 则来自相关但另成一线的 speirein。

items.meaningCN: 分散的行为（-al 构成行为名词）
items.example: Seed dispersal is measured in metres.
items.exampleCN: 种子扩散以米为单位测量。

items.meaningCN: 向不同方向散开（dis- 分开 + spargere 撒）

items.meaning: the state of being scattered; physical dispersion
items.meaningCN: 被分散的状态；物理色散（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: Dispersion of white light produces a spectrum.

items.meaningCN: 有分散倾向的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Sandstone is a dispersive medium for water.
items.exampleCN: 砂岩对水是一种分散性介质。

items.meaning: able to be dispersed in a medium
items.meaningCN: 可分散于介质中的（-ible 表示“能够”）
items.example: The powder is dispersible in cold water.
items.exampleCN: 这种粉末可分散于冷水中。

items.example: Sparse grass covers the dry slope.
items.exampleCN: 稀疏的草覆盖着干旱的坡地。

items.meaningCN: 散布于其他事物之间（inter- 之间 + 撒）
items.example: Wildflowers were interspersed among the wheat.

items.meaning: a sprinkling, hence a slanderous remark
items.meaningCN: 洒水，引申为诽谤（-ion 名词）
items.example: He cast aspersions on the report.
items.exampleCN: 他对这份报告加以中伤。

definition_zh: v. 使气馁；使沮丧；使失去干劲
definition_en: to take away the courage, hope or energy of someone
core_image: 连输几场后全队垂下的头；一封退稿信把气球里的气放掉；长跑最后一圈突然沉下去的肩膀
scene: 接连的失败让全队垂下了头。Repeated defeats dispirit the whole team.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：连输几场之后，全队的勇气和劲头都被抽走了。

pos.zh: 使气馁；使沮丧；使失去干劲

senses.title: Drain the courage
senses.definition: to take away the courage or confidence of someone
senses.definitionCN: （动词）抽走某人的勇气或信心
senses.example: Repeated defeats dispirit the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 接连的失败让全队垂下了头。
senses.why: A row of players with their heads dropping after a loss.
senses.whyCN: 输球后一排垂着头的队员。

senses.title: Make sad and flat
senses.definition: to make someone feel sad and without energy
senses.definitionCN: （动词）让人感到低落、没有力气
senses.example: The grey weeks of rain dispirited her.
senses.exampleCN: 连周灰蒙蒙的雨让她情绪低落。
senses.why: A balloon slowly losing its air on a wet windowsill.
senses.whyCN: 一只在潮湿窗台上慢慢瘪掉的气球。

senses.title: Break the will to continue
senses.definition: to destroy the will of a group to keep going
senses.definitionCN: （动词）打掉一个群体继续做下去的意愿
senses.example: One rejection letter can dispirit a whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 一封退稿信能让全班失去干劲。
senses.why: Shoulders sinking on the last lap of a long race.
senses.whyCN: 长跑最后一圈突然沉下去的肩膀。

intro.en: Dispirit is dis- plus spirit, and spirit goes back to Latin spiritus, breath, from spirare, to breathe; to dispirit someone is to take the breath of courage out of them.
intro.cn: dispirit 由 dis- 加 spirit 构成，而 spirit 追溯到拉丁语 spiritus「气息」，来自 spirare「呼吸」；dispirit 就是把那股勇气之气从人身上抽走。

items.en: Latin spirare means to breathe.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸。

items.en: Spiritus means breath, and then the life within a person.
items.cn: spiritus 意为气息，进而指人内在的生命力。

items.en: Old French espirit carries the sense of soul and courage.
items.cn: 古法语 espirit 带有灵魂与勇气的意思。

items.en: English spirit keeps both breath and inner force.
items.cn: 英语 spirit 同时保留气息与内在力量两义。

items.en: Dispirit appears for draining that inner force away.
items.cn: dispirit 出现，表示把那股内在力量抽走。

items.en: Dispirited and dispiriting are the common everyday forms.
items.cn: dispirited 与 dispiriting 是日常常见形式。

note.en: Dispirit takes the spirit out; its look-alikes keep the same breath root, and its neighbours name other ways of letting the air out of a person.
note.cn: dispirit 是把精神抽走；形近词共用同一个「气息」词根，近义词则是别的给人放气的方式。

to make someone lose hope

examples.en: It was a dispiriting afternoon of rain and delays.
examples.cn: 那是个下雨又延误、令人沮丧的下午。

examples.en: Do not let one failure dispirit you.
examples.cn: 别让一次失败打掉你的劲头。

dict_mnemonic.text: dispirit ＝ dis-（去掉、分离）＋ spirit（精神、气息，拉丁语 spiritus「呼吸」）＝把精神从人身上抽走，「使气馁、使沮丧」；反过来 in-spirit 就是打气，所以 inspire 是鼓舞。

root: 拉丁语 spirare（呼吸）→ spiritus（气息、精神）→ 古法语 espirit → 英语 spirit → dispirit

sensesIntro.en: Air leaving a person: dropped heads after a loss, a flattening balloon and shoulders sinking on the last lap.
sensesIntro.cn: 气从人身上离开：输球后垂下的头、瘪掉的气球与最后一圈沉下去的肩膀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of players with their heads dropping after a loss while a balloon slowly loses its air
core.cn: 核心意象：输球后一排垂着头的队员，同时一只气球慢慢瘪掉

branches.en: Courage taken out of a team.
branches.cn: 从队伍里被抽走的勇气。

branches.en: Mood flattened like a losing balloon.
branches.cn: 像漏气气球一样瘪下去的情绪。

branches.en: The will to finish drained away.
branches.cn: 被抽干的坚持意愿。

branches.en: Both leave a person lower than before.
branches.cn: 两者都让人比先前更低落。

branches.en: Both take away the energy to go on.
branches.cn: 两者都拿走了继续下去的力气。

intro.en: Dispirit is dis- plus the breath root spir-; the same root builds spirit, inspire, respire, conspire and perspire.
intro.cn: dispirit 由 dis- 加气息词根 spir- 构成；同一个词根也造出 spirit、inspire、respire、conspire 与 perspire。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare means to breathe, spiritus breath, and inspirare to breathe into.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸，spiritus 意为气息，inspirare 意为吹入。
